ruling.recommended_action: Record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file (unexcused 3.64 km off-route segment) and send the account to Ryde review for repeated route deviations; no fare adjustment — advise the rider that on a fixed-quote RydeX booking the detour produces no recoverable amount.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a RydeX fixed-quote booking: the fare of $24.93 is composed of listed components (base $3.90, distance $15.06 for 10.68 km, time $4.50 for 17.3 min, waiting $0.00, platform $1.47) [F6], and the billed distance of 10.7 km does not exceed the optimal 10.7 km [F4]. Under RD-2 the non-metered branch refunds only ERP/tolls generated on an unexcused segment and any unpublished post-trip add-on; the extra mileage itself does not move a fixed quote, and no such item appears in the bill [F6]. The recoverable amount is therefore $0.00, so the fare outcome is no_action while the RD-1 breach is recorded [RD-2].

The GPS record shows a genuine unexcused deviation: one off-route segment 14:19–14:26 drove 5.03 km where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, adding 3.64 km and straying up to 1160 m from the optimal route [F3], in a trip that ran 15.2 km against 10.7 km optimal (+4.5 km, +42%) [F1]. RD-1 sets no percentage or absolute km threshold, so this segment violates the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it [RD-1].

RD-5 does not excuse it. There is no in-app chat traffic at all [F7], so no rider message sent before 14:19 authorised a route change or a stop; the driver's post-trip explanation that "the GPS rerouted me" [F8] is a statement, not rider consent, and a driver's claim of agreement cannot supply the rider's own prior message [RD-5]. The segment ground is consent_after_or_none, and the segment counts.

RD-4 does not excuse it either. The only traffic records are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the AYE and CTE [F9][F10], which is neither band 1 nor band 2, so it cannot even corroborate severe congestion under RD-4(b); no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F11] and the weather was fair [F12], so there is no incident-matching "reasonable cause" under RD-4(a) [RD-4].

The driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2 [F14], so this already-breach case makes the deviation repeated and RD-6 requires an account-review referral alongside the ruling; the profile fact is used only for that added action, never to decide the segment [RD-6]. Profile facts are also not used to decide the case against the rider's clean record [F13].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the single chat-log fact (empty) and the driver's statement [F7][F8]; none contains a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so the screen is none — no SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 escalation arises [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

segment_findings.reason: No in-app chat exists at all, so no rider message before the 14:19 segment named a place, agreed to a route or authorised a stop [F7]; the driver's post-trip 'GPS rerouted me' statement is a claim, not rider consent sent before the segment [F8]. With no rider agreement before the segment, RD-5 gives no exemption and the segment counts under RD-1/RD-2 [RD-5][RD-1]. Because the booking is fixed-quote RydeX and the bill carries no detour-linked charge [F4][F6], this counting segment yields a recoverable amount of $0.00 [RD-2].

Accepted: band 4 traffic and no incident means no RD-4 exemption [F9][F10][F11][F12][RD-4]; it still yields no refund on the non-metered branch [RD-2].
Accepted: the recoverable amount on the RydeX branch is nil, so the fare outcome is no_action [F4][F6][FARE-1].
Partially accepted: the RD-1 breach is recorded, but the RD-2 refund stays $0.00 [F3][F6]; the 2 upheld route disputes apply only to the RD-6 account referral, which is granted [F14][RD-6].
Accepted: the bill contains only quoted components and billed distance does not exceed optimal, so no money attaches to the deviation [F4][F6][RD-2].
Accepted as to amount ($0.00 recoverable, [F3][F6][RD-2]), but RD-2's final sentence still records the RD-1 breach, so the segment is not erased.
Accepted: no ERP/toll or unpublished post-trip item appears in the bill, so FARE-1/FARE-2 give nothing [F6][FARE-1].
Accepted in part: no chat means no rider naming or objection [F7], but the same emptiness leaves the segment with no consent at all, so it counts rather than being excused [F8][RD-5].
Accepted: band 4 speed is neither an incident nor band 1–2, so the RD-4 exemption fails and the segment stands unexcused [F9][F10][F11][F12][RD-4].
Accepted: the 2 upheld route disputes are profile facts usable only for the RD-6 account referral, not to decide this segment [F14][RD-6]; the rider's history does not decide it either [F13].
